reference.quote:
# Faster compilation of functions on the Cranelift path (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Time (ms) to compile the compiler itself (out/selfhost/compiler_main.rs, 38886 lines, 9178 functions) with `--no-cache`.
The output .o is the same at every stage.

| Change | -j 1 | -j 4 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Before | 4650 | 2040 |
| Turn off verification of the Cranelift IR (enable it with `ZUSTC_CLIF_VERIFY=1`) | 4140 | |
| Read the syntax tree of a function body only once per body | 3950 | |
| Use FxHash for the number tables; reuse `Context` / `FunctionBuilderContext` | 3810 | |
| Do not re-read the enclosing function each time a closure body is looked up (remember the closure expressions per enclosing function) | about −450 | |
| Change the expression shape hash (`expr_hash`) from a Debug string to a hash that walks the tree (subexpressions are remembered by address) | 3740 | |
| In the cache key, remember the hash of the referenced signatures per function | 3690 | |
| Do not build a String per character when decoding string literals (the 286KB prelude embedded in the compiler) | 3640 | 1740 |

(Measurement noise is about ±200 ms. The first 3 rows are from the previous commit.)

- The expression shape hash built a Debug string for every subexpression recorded during inference, so its cost grew with depth
  (9% of the total). Now it walks the tree once and mixes in the subexpression hashes (the same Debug string gives the same value).
- Of the rest, Cranelift itself is about half (regalloc2 22%, lower 6%, emit 4%), acg code generation is 20%, and type inference is 5%.
- Switching to the `single_pass` regalloc (`ZUSTC_CLIF_FAST_RA=1`) goes from 3640 → 3050 ms, but the .o becomes 43% larger and
  the resulting compiler runs about 40% slower (75 → 104 ms on lexer_main.rs). The default stays backtracking.

reference.quote:
# Smaller IR passed to Cranelift (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Totals of the IR passed to Cranelift, and times, when compiling the compiler itself (out/selfhost/compiler_main.rs) with `--no-cache -j 1`.

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Values | 837,051 | 785,840 (−6%) |
| Stack slots | 74,805 | 62,674 (−16%) |
| Instructions | 972,578 | 997,071 (+3%: from rebuilding slot addresses where they are used) |
| Cranelift compile time | 1420–1490 ms | 1270–1320 ms (−11%) |
| Total | 3850–4020 ms | 3670–3820 ms (−5%) |
| .o of the resulting compiler | 5.20 MB | 4.54 MB (−13%) |

The time for the resulting compiler to compile the same file does not change (2.37–2.52 s). The run times of bench/runtime.py are the same or slightly faster.

- A temporary area that a call wrote its return value into (and a temporary area where a struct / enum was built) is remembered as
  "not used by anyone yet". By-value arguments and `let` use it directly without copying (`Cx::fresh` / `take_fresh`. Values held in
  temporaries that are dropped at the end of the statement are excluded).
- If the tail expression of a function or the expression of a `return` is a call or a struct / enum value, its return value is written
  directly into the function's own sret location (`Cx::ret_call` / `dst_hint`. This is not passed to calls inside arguments).
- clif backend: slot addresses (`stack_addr`) are rebuilt where they are used. Their live ranges get shorter, and they do not become
  Variables that cross ranges (block arguments).
- clif backend: a block is sealed as soon as all instructions that jump into it have been written. Variable values can be resolved on
  the spot, so there are fewer placeholder block arguments. A branch on a constant condition becomes a jump.
- Tried and dropped: turning a copy made of two consecutive 8-byte load / store pairs into one 16-byte (xmm) pair. Instructions went
  down 10% but the time did not change. Reading 16 bytes right after writing 8 bytes defeats store-to-load forwarding, and the
  resulting compiler ran 20% slower.
- Remaining: even for small functions, Cranelift takes about 30 µs per function (50 ms for 1600 functions under 10 instructions).
  Most of the time is regalloc2's live range computation (Env::init) and allocation.
- Environment variables for investigation: `ZUSTC_CLIF_STATS=1` (count per instruction kind), `ZUSTC_CLIF_DUMP=1` (IR), `ZUSTC_CLIF_TIME=1`
  (compile time per function). Each change can be turned off with `ZUSTC_NO_FRESH` / `ZUSTC_NO_RET_DST` / `ZUSTC_CLIF_NO_REMAT` /
  `ZUSTC_CLIF_LATE_SEAL` / `ZUSTC_CLIF_NO_FOLD_BR`.

# Cranelift に渡す IR を小さくする (2026-11-17)

日付: 2026-11-17

自分自身 (out/selfhost/compiler_main.rs) を `--no-cache -j 1` でコンパイルしたときの、Cranelift に渡した IR の合計と時間。

| | 前 | 後 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 値 | 837,051 | 785,840 (−6%) |
| スタックのスロット | 74,805 | 62,674 (−16%) |
| 命令 | 972,578 | 997,071 (+3%: スロットのアドレスを使う所で作り直す分) |
| Cranelift の compile の時間 | 1420〜1490 ms | 1270〜1320 ms (−11%) |
| 全体 | 3850〜4020 ms | 3670〜3820 ms (−5%) |
| できたコンパイラの .o | 5.20 MB | 4.54 MB (−13%) |

できたコンパイラで同じファイルをコンパイルする時間は変わらない (2.37〜2.52 s)。bench/runtime.py の実行時間も同じか少し速い。

- 呼び出しの戻り値を書かせた一時領域 (と struct / enum を組み立てた一時領域) を「まだ誰も使っていない」と覚え、値渡しの引数と
  `let` ではコピーせずにそのまま使う (`Cx::fresh` / `take_fresh`。文の終わりで drop する一時値に入っているものは除く)。
- 関数の末尾の式と `return` の式が呼び出しか struct / enum の値なら、その戻り値を関数自身の sret の場所に直接書かせる
  (`Cx::ret_call` / `dst_hint`。引数の中の呼び出しには渡さない)。
- clif バックエンド: スロットのアドレス (`stack_addr`) は使う所で作り直す。生きている区間が短くなり、区間をまたぐ Variable
  (ブロックの引数) にもならない。
- clif バックエンド: 飛び込む命令をすべて書いたブロックはその場で閉じる (seal)。変数の値をその場で決められるので、ブロックの
  引数の仮置きが減る。条件が定数の分岐は jump にする。
- 試してやめたもの: 8 byte の load / store の組が 2 つ続くコピーを 16 byte (xmm) の 1 組にした。命令は 10% 減ったが時間は
  変わらず、8 byte で書いた直後に 16 byte で読むとストアからの転送が効かず、できたコンパイラの実行が 20% 遅くなった。
- 残り: 小さい関数でも Cranelift は 1 関数あたり約 30 µs かかる (10 命令未満の関数 1600 個で 50 ms)。時間の多くは
  regalloc2 の生存区間の計算 (Env::init) と割り当て。
- 調べるための環境変数: `ZUSTC_CLIF_STATS=1` (命令の種類ごとの数)、`ZUSTC_CLIF_DUMP=1` (IR)、`ZUSTC_CLIF_TIME=1`
  (関数ごとの compile の時間)。それぞれの変更は `ZUSTC_NO_FRESH` / `ZUSTC_NO_RET_DST` / `ZUSTC_CLIF_NO_REMAT` /
  `ZUSTC_CLIF_LATE_SEAL` / `ZUSTC_CLIF_NO_FOLD_BR` で切れる。

# Stop check at type checking to make the LSP faster (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

- check (`zustc check` and the LSP) now stops after acg code generation (type errors are reported there) and does not produce machine code
  (Cranelift / minclif) (`Inline::check_only`). The "checked" marker is "an empty Blob that holds only the relocations to the requested
  generic function instances", stored under a key separate from the build Blob (`CHECK_SALT`) (if a build Blob exists, it also counts as checked).
  `ZUSTC_CHECK_CODEGEN=1` produces machine code too.
- Prelude selection (`select_with`) searched the whole source with `contains` about 80 times. It now searches per item and remembers the
  result by item hash (`PreludeScan`). Until now `SelectCache` was rebuilt on every call, so the per-item memory had no effect;
  Session2 now owns it (`FrontMemo`).
- `lexer::split` is now incremental (`split_inc`): it remembers the previous input and result, reuses the items in the unchanged parts
  before and after (shifting position and line for the part after), and re-splits only the middle. Boundaries are top-level items that
  start after whitespace (impl / trait as a whole). If the end of the middle may be inside a comment or string, or if split fails,
  the whole file is split. tests/split_inc.rs keeps applying random edits to real source and compares each result with a full split.
  `ZUSTC_SPLIT_VERIFY=1` compares every time; `ZUSTC_NO_SPLIT_INC=1` turns it off.

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `zustc check` compiler_main.rs (38886 lines) | 3.6 s | 1.6 s |
| LSP didOpen / didChange, 1000 generated functions (17019 lines, over stdio) | 135 / 12.2 ms | 122 / 9.6 ms |
| LSP didOpen / didChange, compiler_main.rs (editing 1 function) | 2.09 s / 523 ms | 1.63 s / 476 ms |
| split (didChange on 1000 generated functions) | 2.0 ms | 0.6 ms |

Remaining (breakdown of the 476 ms didChange on compiler_main.rs): preprocessing that rewrites the whole file (macro expansion 97 ms,
`mod` flattening 63 ms, moving nested items 47 ms, constructor rewriting 33 ms; each one re-lexes the whole file), Program and references 47 ms,
cache keys and read-back for all functions (9115) 100 ms. All of these rebuild everything, so the next step is to make them incremental per item.

reference.quote:
# Incremental preprocessing per item (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Preprocessing (thread_local! expansion, macro expansion, `mod` flattening, moving nested items, constructor rewriting) is now gathered in
`crates/syntax/src/prep.rs` and remembered per chunk across edits.

- Chunk: a range of lines cut at item boundaries (also inside `mod` / `impl` / `trait`). Cutting into chunks is also incremental
  against the previous run (the boundaries in the unchanged parts before and after are kept; only the middle is re-lexed).
- Every preprocessing step rewrites token by token using data gathered from the whole file (macro definitions, element counts of tuple
  structs and variants, the module tree and `use`, names of nested items), and does not change the number of lines. The gathered data
  depends only on item declarations, so the same data can be gathered from a "skeleton" in which the expressions inside function
  bodies and the initializers of const / static are removed (nested items, `use`, `macro_rules!` and user macro calls inside bodies
  are kept; a body with nothing to keep is removed together with its braces).
- If the whole skeleton is the same as last time, unchanged chunks reuse the previous result, and only the changed chunks are
  preprocessed in a "source where everything else is skeleton" (2.1 MB → 0.31 MB for compiler_main.rs) and then cut out by line.
  When the skeleton changes (a declaration edit), when braces are unbalanced, or when a moved item crosses a chunk boundary, the
  whole file is preprocessed.
- The first call only preprocesses the whole file (a build that preprocesses just once does not create chunk records).
- tests/prep_inc.rs: keeps applying random edits (inside bodies, and anywhere) to the files of examples and crates/core/src bundled with
  `mod`, and each time compares the text, the column shifts and success/failure with full preprocessing (incremental path 156 times,
  full path 364 times). `ZUSTC_PREP_VERIFY=1` compares every time, `ZUSTC_NO_PREP_INC=1` turns it off, `ZUSTC_PREP_LOG=1` prints the path.
- The random edit test found a hoist bug where renaming nested items in broken source never stopped and caused a stack overflow.
  It is fixed (no retry if the rename changes nothing; at most 8 retries).

| Editing 1 function in compiler_main.rs (38886 lines) | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Preprocessing | about 270 ms | 28 ms |
| LSP didChange (over stdio) | 476 ms | 238 ms |

Remaining (didChange 238 ms): cache keys and read-back for all functions (9115) about 100 ms, references 30 ms, Program 18 ms, item summary 8 ms,
split 6 ms, prelude selection 7 ms.

target.quote:
# 前処理をアイテムごとの差分にする (2026-11-17)

日付: 2026-11-17

前処理 (thread_local! の展開・マクロの展開・`mod` を平らにする・入れ子のアイテムの移動・コンストラクタの書き換え) を
`crates/syntax/src/prep.rs` にまとめ、編集をまたいでチャンクごとに覚えるようにした。

- チャンク: アイテムの境界 (`mod` / `impl` / `trait` の中も) で切った行の範囲。チャンクに切るのも前回との差分
  (前後の変わっていない部分の境界はそのまま、間だけを字句解析し直す)。
- どの前処理も、ファイル全体から集めたもの (マクロの定義・タプル struct とバリアントの要素数・モジュールの木と `use`・入れ子の
  アイテムの名前) を使ってトークンごとに書き換え、行の数を変えない。集めるものはアイテムの宣言にしか依らないので、関数の
  本体の中の式と const / static の初期化式を消した「骨組み」から同じものが集まる (本体の中の入れ子のアイテム・`use`・
  `macro_rules!`・ユーザのマクロの呼び出しは残す。残すもののない本体は括弧ごと消す)。
- 骨組みの全体が前回と同じなら、変わっていないチャンクは前回の結果を使い、変わったチャンクだけを「ほかを骨組みにした
  ソース」(compiler_main.rs で 2.1 MB → 0.31 MB) で前処理して行で切り出す。骨組みが変わったとき (宣言の編集)・括弧が
  釣り合っていないとき・移したアイテムがチャンクをまたぐときは全体を前処理する。
- 1 回目の呼び出しは全体を前処理するだけ (1 度しか前処理しないビルドでチャンクの記録を作らない)。
- tests/prep_inc.rs: examples と crates/core/src のファイルを `mod` で束ねたものに乱数の編集 (本体の中と、どこでも) を
  続けて加え、毎回全体の前処理と本文・桁のずれ・成否を比べる (差分の経路 156 回、全体の経路 364 回)。
  `ZUSTC_PREP_VERIFY=1` で毎回比べる、`ZUSTC_NO_PREP_INC=1` で切る、`ZUSTC_PREP_LOG=1` で経路を出す。
- 乱数の編集のテストで、壊れたソースで入れ子のアイテムの名前の変更が止まらず stack overflow になる hoist の不具合が
  見つかったので直した (変えても同じならやり直さない、やり直しは 8 回まで)。

| compiler_main.rs (38886 行) の 1 関数の編集 | 前 | 後 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 前処理 | 約 270 ms | 28 ms |
| LSP didChange (stdio 越し) | 476 ms | 238 ms |

残り (didChange 238 ms): 全関数 (9115) のキャッシュのキーと読み戻し 約 100 ms、参照 30 ms、Program 18 ms、要約 8 ms、
split 6 ms、prelude の選択 7 ms。

reference.quote:
# Incremental cache keys and read-back for check (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Every check built cache keys for all functions (9115 in compiler_main.rs) and read them back from the cache (re-requesting the instances
that had been requested). An LSP session now keeps a record of the previous check (`ChkMemo`) and uses it under the following conditions.

- Declaration fingerprint (`Analysis::iface_fp`): for fn items, the hash of the encoded item summary (signature, closures); for other items,
  their text hashes, in order. Editing only a function body does not change it. Everything a key refers to (referenced signatures, structs,
  consts, the name table) is determined by it.
- If the fingerprint is the same as last time, functions whose body item hash is the same are already checked (no key or read-back needed).
  Requested instances are followed by name, and only those whose body (generic function) item changed are re-requested and checked.
  Anything that failed checking is re-checked every time.
- If the fingerprint changed, checking uses keys and the cache as before, and the record is rebuilt. Only sessions that use the cache
  (the LSP) build the record (a one-shot `zustc check` does not). `ZUSTC_NO_CHECK_MEMO=1` disables it.
- tests/check.rs: keeps adding and removing statements that do or do not cause type errors in the function bodies of examples, and each
  time compares the diagnostics with a check in a fresh session.

| Editing 1 function in compiler_main.rs | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| check (keys and read-back, checking) | about 100 ms | 37 ms (13 functions are re-checked: the edited function and the functions with errors) |
| LSP didChange (over stdio) | 238 ms | 194 ms |

Remaining (didChange 194 ms): preprocessing 30 ms, references 29 ms, Program 17 ms, item summary 9 ms, prelude selection 7 ms, split 6 ms,
other (diagnostics JSON, cfg evaluation, etc.) about 60 ms.

# check のキャッシュのキーと読み戻しを差分にする (2026-11-17)

日付: 2026-11-17

check は毎回、全関数 (compiler_main.rs で 9115) のキャッシュのキーを作り、キャッシュから読み戻して (要求していたインスタンスを
要求し直して) いた。LSP のセッションでは前回の check の記録 (`ChkMemo`) を持ち、次の条件で使う。

- 宣言の指紋 (`Analysis::iface_fp`): fn アイテムは要約 (シグネチャ・クロージャ) の符号のハッシュ、ほかのアイテムはテキストの
  ハッシュを並べたもの。関数の本体だけの編集では変わらない。キーが参照するもの (参照先のシグネチャ・struct・const・
  名前の表) はどれもこれで決まる。
- 指紋が前回と同じなら、本体のアイテムのハッシュが同じ関数は検査済み (キーも読み戻しも要らない)。要求していたインスタンスは
  名前で辿り、本体 (総称関数) のアイテムが変わったものだけを要求し直して検査する。検査に通らなかったものは毎回検査し直す。

reference.quote:
# LSP symbol search (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Added support for `textDocument/documentSymbol` (file outline) and `workspace/symbol` (search by name).

- Symbols are read from the token stream by `symbols` in zust-syntax (no syntax tree is built). Even if the syntax is broken in the middle
  of an edit, it outputs what it can read (a body's `{` is matched by braces alone; if it is not closed, it is cut before the next
  unindented item). Positions are UTF-16 columns in the editor's text itself (before preprocessing).
- What is output: mod / struct / enum / union / trait / impl (the name of `impl Tr for S<T>`) / fn (Method inside impl / trait) / const /
  static / type / macro_rules!, fields of structs and variants, enum variants, and declarations inside extern blocks. detail holds the
  fn signature or the field type. The inside of function bodies is not read.
- workspace/symbol searches the open documents and the .rs files under the initialize rootUri (excluding hidden directories, target, out,
  node_modules). Files that are not open are remembered by modification time and size; only changed ones are re-read.
- Match order: exact → prefix → substring from a word start → substring → characters in order (`nrm` → `norm`). Case-insensitive.
  Up to 256 results. containerName is the enclosing mod / impl / trait.
- Speed (with this directory as the workspace): first call 76 ms (reads 261 files), 3 ms from the second call on.
  Reading the 2854 symbols of compiler_main.rs (2.1 MB) takes 40 ms (the result is kept until the document text changes).
- symbols in tests/lsp.rs, and unit tests in crates/syntax/src/symbols.rs.

# LSP のシンボル検索 (2026-11-17)

日付: 2026-11-17

`textDocument/documentSymbol` (ファイルのアウトライン) と `workspace/symbol` (名前で探す) に対応した。

  エディタのテキストそのもの (前処理の前) の UTF-16 の桁。

# LSP comparison: rust-analyzer / rust-glancer (2026-11-17, `python3 bench/lsp_compare.py --cold`)

Date: 2026-11-17

The 3 LSP servers are run with the same steps (stdio; requests from the server get empty replies):
initialize → initialized → didOpen → query workspace/symbol every 0.1 s until it returns a known name (ready) →
documentSymbol 10 times (median) → workspace/symbol with 5 queries × 5 times (median) → documentSymbol right after a didChange that
adds one function (edit→docsym), and the time until publishDiagnostics arrives (edit→diag, cut off at 20 s). peak RSS is the VmHWM of the
server process; the value in parentheses is the maximum RSS including descendant processes (sampled every 50 ms).

- Target synth: a generated Cargo crate (40 modules, 25 functions each + struct / enum / impl, about 4400 lines). Opens src/m7.rs
- Target zustc: this directory (a Cargo workspace, with dependencies such as cranelift). Opens crates/core/src/driver2.rs
- rust-analyzer 1.100.0 (rustup component). rust-glancer is github.com/rust-glancer/rust-glancer (50dd51a) built with
  `cargo build --release -p rust-glancer` (set with `RUST_GLANCER=<binary>`; needs rust-src).
  `--cold` deletes the rust-glancer index (target/rust_glancer) before measuring

| Target | Server | init | ready | docsym (count) | wsym (found) | edit→docsym | edit→diag | peak RSS (with children) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| synth | zustc | 2.2 ms | 9.6 ms | 0.6 ms (37) | 0.7 ms (5/5) | 2.0 ms | 1.3 ms | 7.5 MB (5.1 MB) |
| synth | zustc (after adding definition / references) | 2.0 ms | 9.7 ms | 0.6 ms (37) | 0.6 ms (5/5) | 1.8 ms | 1.6 ms | 10.7 MB (6.4 MB) |
| synth | rust-analyzer | 18.7 ms | 3243 ms | 1.0 ms (37) | 2.3 ms (5/5) | 8.3 ms | 309 ms | 607 MB (878 MB) |
| synth | rust-glancer | 36.4 ms | 5799 ms | 1.9 ms (38) | 27.0 ms (5/5) | 43.3 ms | - | 16.9 MB (888 MB) |
| zustc | zustc | 2.3 ms | 55.0 ms | 1.8 ms (123) | 3.5 ms (5/5) | 9.7 ms | 7.8 ms | 10.9 MB (9.9 MB) |
| zustc | zustc (after adding definition / references) | 1.9 ms | 91.4 ms | 2.1 ms (123) | 1.3 ms (5/5) | 13.0 ms | 10.4 ms | 29.9 MB (29.4 MB) |
| zustc | rust-analyzer | 23.0 ms | 5954 ms | 3.6 ms (124) | 2.0 ms (5/5) | 26.2 ms | - | 1360 MB (2723 MB) |
| zustc | rust-glancer | 130 ms | 10593 ms | 7.5 ms (113) | 262 ms (5/5) | 48.6 ms | - | 30.7 MB (1798 MB) |

Notes on reading the results:
- The scope of features differs. rust-analyzer does name resolution and type inference across the crate's dependencies, and also supports
  completion, go to definition, and so on. rust-glancer is a lightweight server that builds an index including dependencies (stored on disk).
  zustc lsp checks the open file as a single crate (it does not read Cargo dependencies or other files from `mod x;`), and only reads
  symbols from the token stream. zustc's ready is fast because it builds neither dependencies nor a type index; it only reads the symbols
  of the workspace .rs files.
- edit→diag: for zustc, this is the result of checking only the open file (driver2.rs alone, so it reports errors). rust-analyzer pushes
  its own diagnostics (for the zustc target, none arrived within 20 s). rust-glancer has diagnostics off by default (cargo check is enabled in settings).
- edit→docsym includes processing after receiving didChange (zustc runs check on every didChange, so that time is included).
- rust-analyzer and rust-glancer have large child processes (cargo metadata, rustc, indexing work). rust-glancer's main process is 17–31 MB.
- Differences in symbol counts: rust-glancer counts associated items inside impls etc. differently (the 38 for synth comes from how impl names are output).

reference.quote:
# LSP go to definition and references (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Added support for `textDocument/definition` and `textDocument/references` (`navigate` in zust-syntax). It does no type inference; names are
resolved with the token stream and an item table (symbols flattened, with the owner type and module path attached):

- Locals: function parameters, `let` (visible after the `;`), `for` / `if let` / `while let` (from the next `{`), match arms, closure parameters.
- `x.name`: methods and fields of the type of x (the enclosing impl for `self`; for a local, its type annotation or its `T::..` / `T { .. }` / `T(..)` initializer).
  When the type is unknown, it answers only if there is exactly one member with that name.
- `Q::name`: a member of Q, or an item inside a module named Q. `Self` is the type of the enclosing impl.
- Items: same module → `use` (names, globs, uses of modules brought in by a glob, `as` aliases, the name inside a `use` itself) →
  unique in the workspace → std. std re-exports (`std::sync::Mutex` → sync::poison::mutex) are followed through `pub use`.
  The X in `#[derive(X)]` is the derive macro. Built-in types get no answer.
- Workspace: from the Cargo.toml (members) at the initialize root, it follows each crate root (lib / main / bin / tests / examples /
  benches / build.rs) and `mod x;` (also `#[path]` and inline mods) to decide each file's module path. Items in crates such as tests
  are visible only from the same crate.
- std / core / alloc (rust-src from `rustc --print sysroot`) are indexed in a separate thread after initialize (only definitions and uses are
  kept; the text is discarded and positions are stored as line and column: about 7 MB). `ZUST_ANALYZER_NO_STD=1` turns it off.
- references are the identifiers with the same name (looked up in a per-file name table) whose definition resolves to the same place.
  The inside of `macro_rules!` bodies is not counted (same as rust-analyzer).

# LSP の定義ジャンプと参照 (2026-11-17)

日付: 2026-11-17

`textDocument/definition` と `textDocument/references` に対応した (zust-syntax の `navigate`)。型推論はせず、字句の列と
アイテムの表 (symbols を平らにして、持ち主の型・モジュールのパスを付けたもの) で名前を解決する:

- ローカル: 関数の引数・`let` (`;` の後から見える)・`for` / `if let` / `while let` (次の `{` から)・match の腕・クロージャの引数。
- `x.name`: x の型 (`self` なら囲む impl、ローカルなら型注釈か `T::..` / `T { .. }` / `T(..)` の初期化) のメソッド・フィールド。
  型が分からないときは、同じ名前のメンバが一つだけのときだけ答える。
- `Q::name`: Q のメンバか、Q というモジュールの中のアイテム。`Self` は囲む impl の型。
- アイテム: 同じモジュール → `use` (名前・glob・glob で取り込んだモジュールの use、`as` の別名、`use` の中の名前そのもの) →
  ワークスペースで一つ → std。std の再エクスポート (`std::sync::Mutex` → sync::poison::mutex) は `pub use` をたどる。
  `#[derive(X)]` の X は derive のマクロ。組み込みの型は答えない。
- ワークスペース: initialize の root の Cargo.toml (members) から、各クレートの根 (lib / main / bin / tests / examples /
  benches / build.rs) と `mod x;` (`#[path]`・インラインの mod も) をたどってファイルのモジュールのパスを決める。tests などの
  クレートのアイテムは同じクレートからだけ見える。

  本文は捨てて位置は行と桁で覚える: 約 7 MB)。`ZUST_ANALYZER_NO_STD=1` で切る。

  `macro_rules!` の本体の中は数えない (rust-analyzer と同じ)。

# LSP hover and completion, and memory for large workspaces (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Added support for `textDocument/hover` and `textDocument/completion` (triggered by `.` and `:`). Both look things up in the same index as
definition and references (`navigate` in zust-syntax). Type checking is not used.

- hover: the definition's signature (attributes removed, up to the body's `{`), the enclosing thing (impl / module), and the `///` doc comment before it.
  For locals, the inferred type (`q: Point`); for built-in types, their name.
- Completion:
  - `x.|`: fields and methods of the receiver's type.
  - `Q::|`: members of a type and items of a module. Re-exported names are included too (`std::sync::Mu|`).
  - Otherwise: visible locals, workspace items, names brought in by use, the prelude, common macros, keywords.
  - Filtered by what has been typed so far: prefix, word start. Locals are also matched by characters in order.
- Inferring the receiver's type (held as a string):
  - What can be followed: local type annotations, `let` initializer expressions, parameters, `self`, field types, and return values of methods and functions.
  - Type parameters of the impl are replaced with the receiver's arguments. Example: `unwrap` on `Option<Sig>` → `Sig`, `get` on `HashMap<K, V>` → `Option<&V>`.
  - Expression forms: indexing (`Vec<T>[i]` → T, map → V), `?`, `for x in v`, `if let Some(x) = ..`, `vec![]`, struct expressions, `as T`.
  - Type aliases are expanded together with their type arguments (`LockResult<G>` → `Result<G, ..>`). Deref looks at what is inside the wrapper (`MutexGuard<T>` → T).
  - Methods of implemented / derived traits (`clone`, `map` of `Iterator`, etc.) are also considered.
  - `..Default::default()` and `field: Default::default()` resolve to the `default` of the struct expression's type / the field's type.
- Fixes in the std index:
  - `pub const unsafe fn` and `const trait` could not be read (most methods of core's `impl str` were missing).
  - Files for `sys`, tests and other OSes are not included.
  - Positions are stored on definitions, and module paths / enclosing things are shared: about 21 MB → 10 MB.
- Large workspaces (`ZUST_ANALYZER_MEM_MB`, default 4):
  - Workspace text and token streams are kept only for files up to this total size.
  - Files beyond that are made slim and keep only definitions, `pub use`, and the set of hashes of the names that appear.
  - When references or hover need them, only the files selected by name hash are re-read. Re-read files are kept in an LRU up to the same size.
  - Even with `ZUST_ANALYZER_MEM_MB=0` (everything slim), the answers do not change (parity is the same). references get slower: 9 → 31 ms per call on the zustc target.

# LSP の hover と補完、大きいワークスペースのメモリ (2026-11-17)

日付: 2026-11-17

`textDocument/hover` と `textDocument/completion` (`.` と `:` で起動) に対応した。どちらも定義・参照と同じ索引
(zust-syntax の `navigate`) から引く。型検査は使わない。

- hover: 定義のシグネチャ (属性を外し、本体の `{` の前まで)・囲むもの (impl / モジュール)・その前の `///` の doc コメント。
  ローカルは推定した型 (`q: Point`)、組み込みの型はその名前。
- 補完:
  - `x.|`: 受け手の型のフィールドとメソッド。
  - `Q::|`: 型のメンバとモジュールのアイテム。re-export した名前も入れる (`std::sync::Mu|`)。
  - それ以外: 見えるローカル・ワークスペースのアイテム・use した名前・prelude・よく使うマクロ・予約語。
  - 打った途中までで絞る: 前方一致・語の頭。ローカルは文字の順でも合わせる。
- 受け手の型の推定 (文字列で持つ):
  - たどれるもの: ローカルの型注釈・`let` の初期化の式・引数・`self`、フィールドの型、メソッドと関数の戻り値。
  - impl の型引数は受け手の引数で置き換える。例: `Option<Sig>` の `unwrap` → `Sig`、`HashMap<K, V>` の `get` → `Option<&V>`。
  - 式の形: 添字 (`Vec<T>[i]` → T、map → V)、`?`、`for x in v`、`if let Some(x) = ..`、`vec![]`、構造体の式、`as T`。
  - 型の別名は型引数ごと展開する (`LockResult<G>` → `Result<G, ..>`)。Deref は包みの中身を見る (`MutexGuard<T>` → T)。
  - impl / derive された trait のメソッド (`clone`、`Iterator` の `map` など) も見る。
  - `..Default::default()` と `field: Default::default()` は、構造体の式の型・フィールドの型の `default` にする。
- std の索引で直したところ:
  - `pub const unsafe fn` と `const trait` を読めていなかった (core の `impl str` のメソッドの大半が落ちていた)。
  - `sys`・テスト・ほかの OS 向けのファイルを入れない。
  - 位置は定義に、モジュールのパス・囲むものは共有して持つ: 約 21 MB → 10 MB。
- 大きいワークスペース (`ZUST_ANALYZER_MEM_MB`、既定 4):
  - ワークスペースの本文と字句の列は、合計がこの大きさまでのファイルの分だけ持つ。
  - 超えた分のファイルは slim にして、定義・`pub use`・出てくる名前のハッシュの集合だけを持つ。
  - 参照・hover で要るときは、名前のハッシュで選んだファイルだけ読み直す。読み直したものは同じ大きさまで LRU で覚える。
  - `ZUST_ANALYZER_MEM_MB=0` (全部 slim) でも答えは変わらない (parity は同じ)。参照は遅くなる: zustc の対象で 1 回 9 → 31 ms。

# Closing the remaining references mismatches (2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Looked at the mismatches from `python3 bench/lsp_parity.py --detail` and aligned the counting with rust-analyzer.

- References to a type now include `Self` inside that type's impls (`-> Option<Self>` in `impl Enc for Vec<T>` is a reference to Vec).
- Pattern and parameter bindings (`let (a, concrete) = ..` / `fn f(concrete: T)` / `for (i, x) in` / `|a, b|`) resolve to the binding itself.
  Before, they were counted as references to a function with the same name, `concrete`.
- If Q in `Q::name` is an unknown name (`syn::Pat` from an external crate, `Delimiter::None` from `use proc_macro2::Delimiter`), no answer is given.
  Before, `None` resolved to Option's None and `Pat` to the workspace's Pat.
- cfg:
  - Items excluded by `#[cfg(..)]` are removed from definitions, and the names inside them are not counted. If the cursor is inside one, no answer is given.
  - features are followed per crate, starting from default in `[features]` of Cargo.toml.

reference.quote:
# Mutation testing (cargo-mutants, 2026-11-17)

Date: 2026-11-17

Installed with `cargo install cargo-mutants --locked` (27.1.0), and run with `bench/mutants.sh`.

- Settings and scope:
  - Settings are in `.cargo/mutants.toml`. Builds use `profile.mutants` (the same optimization as release, with incremental builds).
  - Not mutated: CLI argument handling, build.rs, test and bench code, Debug / Display.
  - There are 18,240 mutants in total. Each one takes a few seconds to 1 minute of tests, so not all of them are run.
- Narrowing the scope:
  - `bench/mutants.sh diff [BASE]`: only mutants on lines in the diff from BASE (default origin/main). For checking changes.
  - `bench/mutants.sh pkg zust-ide`: per crate.
  - `bench/mutants.sh file crates/ide/src/symbols.rs -- -F match_score -j 2`: specify the file, the function name, and the parallelism.
  - `bench/mutants.sh list ...`: only show the count.
  - Everything after `--` is passed to cargo mutants as-is (`--shard 1/8`, etc.).
- Packages used for testing:
  - Mutants only in crates/ide / crates/analyzer: the tests of zust-ide and zust-analyzer. 2–3 seconds each.
  - Others: the tests of the whole workspace (many tests of the compiler layers are in the root tests/). About 1 minute each.
- The timeout is the larger of 3 times the baseline test time or 180 seconds.
- Results go in `mutants.out/` (missed.txt lists the mutants the tests did not catch).

Results of trial runs:

| Target | Mutants | Caught | Missed | Time (-j 2) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `match_score` (ide) | 25 | 16 → 24 | 9 → 1 | 87 seconds |
| `KeyState::done` (base) | 7 | 5 | 2 | 5 minutes |

- The 9 missed mutants in `match_score` were in the word-start check (separators other than `_`); the tests only looked at `_`.
  Added cases for camelCase, `::`, whitespace, and names with consecutive uppercase letters.
- The remaining 1 (`i > 0` → `i >= 0`) is an equivalent mutant: i = 0 returns earlier as a prefix match, so it never gets there.
- The 2 in `KeyState::done` are in how the hash is mixed (`^` → `|`, `<<` → `>>`). A cache key works as long as the same input gives
  the same value, so functional tests cannot see this (it degrades collision resistance).

`cfg_pred`, `macro_bodies`, etc.). The golden tests (fixtures) only exercised common code patterns and did not check boundaries or one side of branches.

    `index_type` / `type_head` / `name_hash` (known FNV-1a values) / `mod_score` / `use_module` / `lib_rank`.
  - cfg: `any` / `all` / `not` / `target_os` / `target_family` / `unix` / `windows` / `miri` / unknown predicates.
  - The range of `macro_rules!` bodies (`{}` / `()` / inside a function / unclosed), the use tree (nested, `as`, glob, `self`).
  - Locals: let / for / if let / while let / match arms and guards / or patterns / closures / parameter patterns /
    the lifetime of bindings inside blocks. The binding checks (`pat_binding` / `fn_param` / `arm_binding`) in both positive and negative cases.
  - Types: annotations (`&'static P`, `&mut a::b::P`), `T(..)`, `T { .. }`, `U::new()`, `a::b::P`.
  - 16 derive methods (`clone` / `default` / `eq` / `ne` / `fmt` / `partial_cmp` / `lt` .. / `hash`).

- Bugs found by the tests (fixed):
  - g in the match guard `S { f: g } if g > 0 =>` was not resolved (the binding was introduced at `=>`). It now looks ahead to see whether

  - The type of v in `let v = a::b::P;` became `b` (the module name was used as the type). Same for `a::b::T(..)` / `m::f()`.

  - In the or pattern `(m, 0) | (0, m)`, m resolved to the later occurrence. It now resolves to the earlier one, as in rust-analyzer.
  - In `apply_cfg`, when recounting the derives of items excluded by cfg, the excluded ranges had not been added yet.
  - The LSP looked for `#[path = "x.rs"] mod m;` directly under a file at `<file name>/x.rs` (rustc looks from the directory containing
    the file). Because of this, navigate_tests.rs was not read, and zustc's references match appeared to drop from 78% → 58%.

  The remaining references differences are things rust-analyzer counts inside cfg-excluded items, in generated files in OUT_DIR, and in
  lexer.rs, which is shared with build.rs.

After adding the tests, the run was redone on just the 967 mutants of the helper functions above (37 functions) (`-F` for the function names, `-j 3`, 82 minutes.
For the ones still missed, more tests were added and the run was repeated with `--iterate`):

| | Caught | Missed | Timeouts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before adding (the same functions, from the partial full run) | — | 441 | — |
| Run 1 (967 mutants) | 715 | 213 | 39 |
| Run 2 (the remaining 249 with `--iterate`) | 749 | 179 | 39 |

- Timeouts are mutants such as `+=` → `-=` that never finish (the test hangs, so this is the same as caught).
- Most of the remaining 179 are mutants that do not change the result:
  - Boundary `<` → `<=` (`sym` / `ident` return false outside the range, so the result is the same).
  - Early exits (the first exclusion in `arm_binding` / `pat_binding`, the cutoff at `{` / `;` in `guard_arrow`): the later scan or
    the range check in `arm_pat` gives the same answer. They exist for speed.
  - The scan for `>` in `generic_names`: `targs` splits the result again, so it is the same. It exists to avoid copying the rest of the file.

# Add rename / signatureHelp / documentHighlight to the LSP (2026-11-18)

Date: 2026-11-18

All three are built on the existing definition / references / signature parts (`prepare_rename` / `rename` /
`signature_help` in `crates/ide/src/navigate.rs`, and the handlers in `crates/analyzer/src/lib.rs`).

- **rename** (with `prepareProvider`):
  - Rewrites the reference locations. For a trait method, it also rewrites the impl methods.
  - Struct shorthand changes shape: renaming a field turns `S { x }` → `S { new: x }`; renaming a local turns
    `S { x }` → `S { x: new }`. It also rewrites inside format captures `"{x}"`.
  - On the B in `use a::B;`, it adds an alias (`use a::B as New;`, plus the B uses in that file). This is the same shape as rust-analyzer.
  - Refused (error `RequestFailed` with a reason): keywords, built-in types, library definitions (except when on a use
    name), file modules (`mod x;`, because the file name would also change), methods generated by derive, and strings that are not valid names.
- **signatureHelp**: the call enclosing the cursor: `f(..)` / `x.m(..)` / `T::f(..)` / `f::<T>(..)` / tuple struct `T(..)`.
  Parameter ranges are in UTF-16 columns. For method calls, self is not counted as a parameter (same as rust-analyzer). Inside an array
  or `vec![..]` within the arguments, it still answers with the outer call. It does not answer inside a declaration `fn f(..)`.
- **documentHighlight**: references within the same file.

Added the comparison against rust-analyzer to `bench/lsp_parity.py` (rename: is the set of edits the same; signatureHelp:
does it contain the name, the parameter count, and the active parameter; documentHighlight: the count):

| Target | Feature | zustc | rust-analyzer |
|---|---|---|---|
| synth | rename | 100% | 100% |
| synth | signatureHelp | 100% (answered 100%) | 100% (answered 95%) |
| synth | documentHighlight | 100% | 100% |
| zustc | rename | 82% (refusals also match, 23/23) | 100% |
| zustc | signatureHelp | 89% (answered 85%) | 100% (answered 95%) |
| zustc | documentHighlight | 85% | 100% |

- Median time (target zustc): rename 1.3 ms (rust-analyzer 0.9), signatureHelp 1.3 ms (rust-analyzer 0.4).
  Time and match for the other features are unchanged (references 14.5 ms, rust-analyzer 26.4 ms).
- Remaining differences:
  - rename and documentHighlight: inside items excluded by cfg, which rust-analyzer counts (same as for references).
    For `Default::default`, rust-analyzer rewrites 1,273 locations, reaching into dependency crates (zustc rewrites the 16 in the workspace).
  - signatureHelp: no answer for std trait methods (`extend`) or for closure calls (`body_hash(..)`).
- The first measurement gave rename 71% and signatureHelp 26%. Fixed after comparing with rust-analyzer:
  self in method calls (parameter count and active parameter were off by 1), rename on a use name (make an alias),
  and refusing rename on `std::sync::Mutex` written as a path.

# Closing the remaining differences from rust-analyzer: cfg, rename of trait impls, signatureHelp (2026-11-18)

Date: 2026-11-18

- **Inside items excluded by cfg**: matched the behavior confirmed by querying rust-analyzer on a small workspace.
  - Inside excluded items (functions, impls, structs, enums, consts, types, traits, inline mods, statement cfg), rust-analyzer still
    resolves paths to items visible from the outer scope (`used()` / `P` / `sub::deep` / `crate::P` / names imported with use),
    and answers definition / references / hover for them. It does not answer for locals, fields, methods (`p.get()` / `s.x`), associated items (`P::new`),
    or the name of the excluded item itself. Previously zustc excluded everything that was excluded.
  - `def_at` looks up tokens in excluded regions with `inactive_def_at` and answers only the cases above. references, rename and hover also go through this.
  - `apply_cfg`: unset cfgs used to be treated as "true"; now they are "false", as in rustc
    (`no_global_oom_handling` / `miri` / `doc` / unknown `key = ".."`). Added support for `target_arch` / `target_pointer_width` /
    `target_endian` / `target_env` / `target_vendor` / `target_has_atomic` / `panic`. `test` and
    `debug_assertions` are treated as true, same as rust-analyzer.
- **Renaming a method of a trait impl** (`fn default` in `impl Default for S`): rust-analyzer rewrites 1,273 locations, reaching into the std
  declaration and the sources of dependency crates (an edit that breaks the build as-is). zustc does not match this:
  - Trait in the workspace: re-resolve from the trait declaration, and rewrite the declaration, all impls, and the calls.
  - Trait from a library or external crate: refuse with a reason (because the declaration cannot be changed).
- **signatureHelp**:
  - No answer for `st.extend(..)` (`Vec<String>`) because there were two candidates, std's `impl Extend<T> for Vec` and `impl Extend<&T> for Vec`,
    and neither was chosen. For methods with the same owner and same name in the same file, the first one (the generic one) is now used.
    definition / hover now answer in the same way.
  - Closure call `h(..)` (`let h = |name: &str| -> Option<Key> { .. }`): the signature is `impl Fn(name: &str) -> Option<Key>`
    (if the return type is not written, the type of the body expression). rust-analyzer expands `Key` to `u128`.
  - Attached doc comments as `documentation`, same as rust-analyzer.
- **Expression types for literals**: `"a"` → &str, `'c'` → char, `b"x"` → &[u8], `b'x'` → u8, `1u8` / `2.0f32` / `1_000usize`,
  `true` → bool. Only when the whole expression is a literal (the 1 in `x + 1` is not an expression type). Numbers without a suffix (`0` / `1.5`)
  get their type from usage (rust-analyzer makes acc in `let mut acc = 0; acc = add(acc, x_i64)` an i64), so no type is given.

Results (`python3 bench/lsp_parity.py`, target zustc; synth stays at 100% for everything):

| Feature | Before | After | rust-analyzer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| references (count match) | 78% | 92% | 100% |
| documentHighlight | 85% | 100% | 100% |
| rename (edit match) | 82% | 94% | 100% |
| signatureHelp | 89% (answered 85%) | 100% (answered 95%) | 100% (answered 95%) |
| Median time refe / rena / sign (ms) | 14.5 / 1.3 / 1.3 | 14.2 / 1.3 / 1.2 | 25.0 / 0.8 / 0.5 |

fixture (`python3 bench/ide_golden_ra.py`): definition 460 → 462/467, references 584 → 606/629 (93% → 96%),
hover 612 → 614/636.

Remaining differences: rename of `default` (the deliberate refusal above). references for `u8` / `Key` (rust-analyzer also counts inside the
generated files in OUT_DIR, and inside lexer.rs, which is shared with build.rs). hover on `ZUSTC_INLINE_LOG` (inside a string).

# rust-analyzer との残りの違いを詰める: cfg・trait の impl の rename・signatureHelp (2026-11-18)

日付: 2026-11-18

- **cfg で外れたアイテムの中**: rust-analyzer に小さいワークスペースで聞いて確かめた振る舞いに合わせた。
  - rust-analyzer は外れたアイテム (関数・impl・struct・enum・const・type・trait・インラインの mod・文の cfg) の中も、
    外側のスコープから見えるアイテムへのパス (`used()` / `P` / `sub::deep` / `crate::P` / use で取り込んだ名前) は解決して、
    definition / references / hover に答える。ローカル・フィールド・メソッド (`p.get()` / `s.x`)・関連アイテム (`P::new`)・
    外れたアイテムの名前そのものには答えない。前の zustc は外れたものを全部除いていた。
  - `def_at` が外れた所のトークンを `inactive_def_at` で引き、上の範囲だけを答える。references・rename・hover もこれを通る。
  - `apply_cfg`: 設定されていない cfg を「成り立つ」としていたのを、rustc と同じく「成り立たない」にした
    (`no_global_oom_handling` / `miri` / `doc` / 知らない `key = ".."`)。`target_arch` / `target_pointer_width` /
    `target_endian` / `target_env` / `target_vendor` / `target_has_atomic` / `panic` を分かるようにした。`test` と
    `debug_assertions` は rust-analyzer と同じく成り立つとする。
- **trait の impl のメソッドの rename** (`impl Default for S` の `fn default`): rust-analyzer は std の宣言と依存のクレートの
  ソースまで 1,273 か所書き換える (そのままでは壊れる書き換え)。zustc はここは合わせず、
  - trait がワークスペースのもの: trait の宣言から引き直して、宣言・全部の impl・呼び出しを書き換える。
  - ライブラリ・外部のクレートの trait: 理由を付けて断る (宣言の方を変えられないので)。
- **signatureHelp**:
  - `st.extend(..)` (`Vec<String>`) に答えなかったのは、std の `impl Extend<T> for Vec` と `impl Extend<&T> for Vec` の
    2 つの候補でどちらも選ばなかったため。同じファイルの同じ持ち主・同じ名前のメソッドなら先のもの (総称的なもの) にした。
    definition / hover も同じく答えるようになった。
  - クロージャの呼び出し `h(..)` (`let h = |name: &str| -> Option<Key> { .. }`): `impl Fn(name: &str) -> Option<Key>` を
    シグネチャにする (戻り値を書いていなければ本体の式の型)。rust-analyzer は `Key` を展開して `u128` にする。
  - rust-analyzer と同じく doc コメントを `documentation` に付けた。
- **式の型のリテラル**: `"a"` → &str、`'c'` → char、`b"x"` → &[u8]、`b'x'` → u8、`1u8` / `2.0f32` / `1_000usize`、
  `true` → bool。式全体がリテラルのときだけ (`x + 1` の 1 は式の型ではない)。接尾辞のない数 (`0` / `1.5`) は、
  使い方で型が決まる (rust-analyzer は `let mut acc = 0; acc = add(acc, x_i64)` の acc を i64 にする) ので型にしない。

結果 (`python3 bench/lsp_parity.py`、zustc を対象。synth は全部 100% のまま):

| 機能 | 前 | 後 | rust-analyzer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

# Widening the LSP comparison and closing the remaining differences (2026-11-18)

Date: 2026-11-18

**Fixed the benchmark (`bench/lsp_parity.py`)**:

- Four targets: synth (40 generated modules), fixture (the ide test workspace, new), zustc (driver2.rs), and
  ide (navigate.rs, new: a file in a different style with many lexical parts).
- Wait until rust-analyzer is ready: it keeps analyzing types after names resolve, so watch `$/progress` and
  `experimental/serverStatus` (quiescent) and wait until the work is done (before, rust-analyzer completion looked like 0% on fixture).
- Times are p50 and p90. Also the time from startup until names resolve and until work is done, and peak memory (RSS of the server and its child processes).
- "Match average" (the average of the per-feature match) as a single number.
- `--json bench/lsp_parity.json` saves the zustc numbers, and `--compare` adds columns with the difference from the previous run (points for match, ms for time).
- `--detail` also prints differences in workspace/symbol and documentSymbol. `--detail-out` writes them to a file.

**Fixed** (each one was matched only after confirming the behavior by querying rust-analyzer on a small workspace):

- **std re-exports were missing**: `FileIndex::library` collected `pub use` after discarding the token stream.
  This affects completion of `use std::sync::Mu|` and resolution of paths such as `std::collections::HashMap`.
- **hover on string and char literals**: `&'static str` and the value (same shape as rust-analyzer).
- **`include!` and OUT_DIR**: also read the files of `include!("x.rs")` and `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/x.rs"))`
  (OUT_DIR is the newest build script output under target).
- **`Self`**: definition is the type name in the impl header; references are that and the `Self` in the same impl (same as rust-analyzer).
- **Items inside functions** (`fn walk` written inside `fn new`) and the static in **`thread_local! { static X }`** become definitions
  (things inside thread_local are not shown in documentSymbol, same as rust-analyzer).
- **documentSymbol kinds**: associated functions that do not take `self` are Function, statics are Constant, and `extern "C" { .. }` items are children of a
  block symbol (Namespace).
- **workspace/symbol**: matched rust-analyzer's rules.
  - First search only types (struct / enum / union / trait / type and crate names); if none, search everything (excluding fields, and members inside impls and
    trait impls).
  - Matches where the characters appear in order. A query that contains uppercase letters is case-sensitive. Up to 128 results, in (lowercase) name order.
  - Crate names: package targets (lib / bin / tests / benches / examples / build.rs), dependencies in Cargo.lock, and std.
  - Also aliases from `use a::B as C` and re-exports from `pub use`.
- **On keywords such as `fn`**: definition goes to that name. references / documentHighlight on `fn` give the function's exits
  (`fn`, `return`, `?`, and the last expression; if the last expression is a match / if, the last expression of each match arm and each block).
- **Types of closure parameters**: parameters of `v.iter().filter(|d| ..)` / `opt.map(|x| ..)` / `fold(0, |acc, x| ..)` get the element type of the receiver
  (a reference for filter and similar). This affects completion, hover and definition.
- **rename**: an `enum E { A, B }` declaration was mistaken for struct shorthand and turned into `A: new`. If there is nothing to rewrite, refuse.

**Made faster**:

- references: for each candidate identifier, name candidates were searched across all definitions (more than 100,000, including std). Now a name
  index (`named`) is built for the duration of one query. For a member reference `Q::name`, if Q is a concrete type that is not the owner, it is not resolved at all.
  In-server time 2.5 ms → 0.5 ms (synth).
- documentHighlight: it used to search references across the whole workspace and then filter; now it searches only that file (zustc: 14.9 → 1.2 ms).
- hover / signatureHelp: when re-reading a std file, read only the text (no index is built).
- Responses are written in one write (splitting header and body caused 3 writes because of per-line stdout flushes).

Results (`python3 bench/lsp_parity.py --compare`, zustc / rust-analyzer; the match-average difference is versus before this work):

| Target | Match average zustc | rust-analyzer | Diff | references p50 zustc / ra (ms) | Startup to names / memory zustc | rust-analyzer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| synth | 99.7% | 99.1% | +1.3 pts | 0.7 / 0.7 | 13 ms / 17 MB | 2689 ms / 868 MB |
| fixture | 97.3% | 95.6% | +15.4 pts | 0.9 / 0.9 | 7 ms / 17 MB | 332 ms / 833 MB |
| zustc | 96.3% | 95.5% | +4.3 pts | 5.4 / 22.4 | 139 ms / 53 MB | 4932 ms / 2368 MB |
| ide | 96.0% | 97.5% | +8.4 pts | 3.6 / 2.3 | 170 ms / 53 MB | 5391 ms / 1874 MB |

- workspace/symbol is 100% on all four (before: 62–87%), documentSymbol is 100% including kinds, and documentHighlight is 100%.
- rust-analyzer's match average is not 100% because places where it did not answer (such as "answered" for definition) are counted.
- The large difference on fixture includes the share where the old comparison queried before rust-analyzer finished analyzing (completion at 0%).
- Completion for `x.|` on ide looks like -10 points, but navigate.rs changed during the work, so the compared positions are different.
- Remaining differences:
  - rename of `Default::default` (rust-analyzer rewrites into dependency crates; deliberately refused), and
    on Point in `use a::{Point as Pt}` (rust-analyzer changes only the alias and not the uses; zustc changes the definition).
  - references for `Key`: rust-analyzer counts a different `Key` inside lexer.rs, which is shared with build.rs.
  - Completion on receivers of unknown type (`x.as_str()` and so on), signatureHelp for std methods (`map(` and so on), and methods of numeric
    types (`wrapping_sub`: generated by macros in core).

# LSP の比べ方を広げ、残りの違いを詰める (2026-11-18)

日付: 2026-11-18

**ベンチマーク (`bench/lsp_parity.py`) を直した**:

- 対象を 4 つに: synth (生成した 40 モジュール)・fixture (ide のテストのワークスペース、新)・zustc (driver2.rs)・
  ide (navigate.rs、新: 字句の部品が多い別の書き方のファイル)。
- rust-analyzer の準備ができるまで待つ: 名前が引けた後も型の解析を続けているので、`$/progress` と
  `experimental/serverStatus` (quiescent) を見て、作業が終わるまで待つ (前は fixture で rust-analyzer の補完が 0% に見えていた)。
- 時間は p50 と p90。起動から名前が引けるまで・作業が終わるまでの時間と、メモリの最大 (サーバと子のプロセスの RSS)。
- 「一致の平均」(機能ごとの一致の平均) を 1 つの数に。
- `--json bench/lsp_parity.json` で zustc の数字を残し、`--compare` で前回との差 (一致は点、時間は ms) を列に足す。
- `--detail` で workspace/symbol・documentSymbol の違いも出す。`--detail-out` でファイルに。

**直したもの** (どれも rust-analyzer に小さいワークスペースで聞いて、振る舞いを確かめてから合わせた):

- **std の再エクスポートが入っていなかった**: `FileIndex::library` が字句の列を捨ててから `pub use` を集めていた。
  `use std::sync::Mu|` の補完、`std::collections::HashMap` などのパスの解決に効く。
- **文字列・文字のリテラルの hover**: `&'static str` と値 (rust-analyzer と同じ形)。
- **`include!` と OUT_DIR**: `include!("x.rs")` と `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/x.rs"))` のファイルも読む
  (OUT_DIR は target の下のビルドスクリプトの出力のいちばん新しいもの)。
- **`Self`**: definition は impl の見出しの型の名前、references はそれと同じ impl の中の `Self` (rust-analyzer と同じ)。
- **関数の中のアイテム** (`fn walk` を `fn new` の中に書いたもの) と **`thread_local! { static X }`** の static を定義にする
  (thread_local の中のものは rust-analyzer と同じく documentSymbol には出さない)。
- **documentSymbol の種類**: `self` を取らない関連関数は Function、static は Constant、`extern "C" { .. }` はブロックの
  記号 (Namespace) の子に。
- **workspace/symbol**: rust-analyzer の決まりに合わせた。
  - まず型 (struct / enum / union / trait / type とクレートの名前) だけを探し、なければ全部 (フィールド・impl・trait の impl の
    中のメンバは除く) から。
  - 文字が順に出てくるもの。大文字を含む問い合わせは大文字と小文字を区別する。名前の (小文字の) 順に 128 個まで。
  - クレートの名前: パッケージのターゲット (lib / bin / tests / benches / examples / build.rs) と Cargo.lock の依存と std。
  - `use a::B as C` の別名と `pub use` の再エクスポートも。
- **`fn` などのキーワードの上**: definition はその名前に。`fn` の上の references / documentHighlight は関数の出口
  (`fn`・`return`・`?`・最後の式。最後の式が match / if なら各腕・各ブロックの最後の式)。
- **クロージャの引数の型**: `v.iter().filter(|d| ..)` / `opt.map(|x| ..)` / `fold(0, |acc, x| ..)` の引数に、受け手の要素の型
  (filter などは参照)。補完・hover・定義に効く。
- **rename**: `enum E { A, B }` の宣言を構造体の省略形と取り違えて `A: new` にしていた。書き換える所がなければ断る。

**速くしたもの**:

- references: 候補の識別子ごとに名前の候補を全部の定義 (std を含めて 10 万個以上) から探していた。問い合わせ 1 回の間の
  名前の索引 (`named`) にした。メンバの参照で `Q::name` の Q が持ち主でない具体的な型なら解決もしない。
  サーバの中で 2.5 ms → 0.5 ms (synth)。
- documentHighlight: ワークスペース全体の参照を探してから絞っていたのを、そのファイルだけ探すように (zustc で 14.9 → 1.2 ms)。
- hover / signatureHelp: std のファイルを読み直すとき、本文だけにした (索引は作らない)。
- 応答は 1 回の書き込みに (ヘッダと本文を分けると stdout の行ごとの flush で 3 回になっていた)。

結果 (`python3 bench/lsp_parity.py --compare`、zustc / rust-analyzer。一致の平均の差は今回の前との差):

| 対象 | 一致の平均 zustc | rust-analyzer | 差 | references p50 zustc / ra (ms) | 起動から名前まで / メモリ zustc | rust-analyzer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| synth | 99.7% | 99.1% | +1.3 点 | 0.7 / 0.7 | 13 ms / 17 MB | 2689 ms / 868 MB |
| fixture | 97.3% | 95.6% | +15.4 点 | 0.9 / 0.9 | 7 ms / 17 MB | 332 ms / 833 MB |
| zustc | 96.3% | 95.5% | +4.3 点 | 5.4 / 22.4 | 139 ms / 53 MB | 4932 ms / 2368 MB |
| ide | 96.0% | 97.5% | +8.4 点 | 3.6 / 2.3 | 170 ms / 53 MB | 5391 ms / 1874 MB |

- workspace/symbol は 4 つとも 100% (前は 62〜87%)、documentSymbol は種類まで 100%、documentHighlight は 100%。
- rust-analyzer の一致の平均が 100% でないのは、答えなかった所 (definition の「答えた」など) を数えているため。
- fixture の差が大きいのは、前の比べ方では rust-analyzer の解析が終わる前に聞いていた (補完が 0%) 分も入っている。
- ide の `x.|` の補完は -10 点に見えるが、作業の間に navigate.rs が変わって比べる位置が違う。
- 残りの違い:
  - rename の `Default::default` (rust-analyzer は依存のクレートの中まで書き換える。わざと断る) と、
    `use a::{Point as Pt}` の Point の上 (rust-analyzer は別名だけを変えて使う所を変えない。zustc は定義を変える)。
  - references の `Key`: build.rs と共有する lexer.rs の中の別の `Key` を rust-analyzer が数える。
  - 型が分からない受け手の補完 (`x.as_str()` など)・std のメソッドの signatureHelp (`map(` など)・数の型の
    メソッド (`wrapping_sub`: core ではマクロで作る)。

# Closing gaps in type inference (2026-11-18)

Date: 2026-11-18

Using rust-analyzer's hover types as the ground truth, compared 39 commonly written expressions (iterator chains, Option / Result, HashMap, tuples,
turbofish, numeric-type methods). Before, only 7 of 17 matched (`Option<U>` /
`Option<Iter<'_, ..>::Item>` / no type shown); now all 39 are the same (including how closure types are displayed). This comparison is kept as
`type_inference_like_rust_analyzer` in `crates/analyzer/tests/lsp.rs` (it uses the real std).

- **Iterator element types** (`iter_item`): `Iter<'_, T>` → &T, `IterMut` → &mut T, `IntoIter` → T, HashMap's
  `Iter<'_, K, V>` → (&K, &V), `Map<I, impl FnMut(..) -> R>` → R, `FilterMap` / `FlatMap` / `Flatten` / `Enumerate` /
  `Zip` / `Cloned` / `Copied` / `Rev` / `Skip` .., `Chars` / `Lines` / `Range` ... Replaces the projections `Self::Item` / `<A as Iterator>::Item` /
  `U::IntoIter` (`norm_proj`).
- **Deciding method type arguments from closures**: definitions carry (argument index, type argument, return shape, argument shape) taken from
  signature bounds such as `F: FnMut(Self::Item) -> B` (`fn_bounds`). The return type of the closure in the call's arguments is fitted to the shape
  (`unify`: `Option<U>` and `Option<char>` → U = char), which decides the result type of `map` / `and_then` / `filter_map` / `fold`.
  An argument whose type is the type argument itself (`zip(other: U)`) uses the type of the argument expression. Turbofish (`collect::<Vec<_>>()` /
  `sum::<u32>()` / `parse::<u8>()`) goes to the first type argument (`_` is the element type).
- **Types of closure parameters**: from the parameter shape of the signature's `F: FnOnce(&T)` (m in `KEY.with(|m| ..)` is &T; the second one of `fold` is
  the element). If unknown, the element type of the receiver. Also tuple patterns `|(k, v)|` / `for (i, x) in` / `let (a, b) =`.
- **Expression types**: tuple expressions `(a, b)`, tuple indexing `x.0` (and indexing after it, `u.1[0]`), parenthesized expressions, array expressions `[a, b]` / `[x; n]`,
  unit struct values, `match` / `if` / block expressions (the type of the last expression of the match arm or block), references `&x`, calls to local closures,
  and dropping lifetime names (`&'a str` → `&str`).
- **impls inside std macros**: `impl Iterator` for slice `Iter` and similar live inside core macros and are not visible, so the iterator types are given
  Iterator directly. For numeric-type methods (`wrapping_sub` / `checked_sub` / `count_ones` ..), the items in the bodies of core's `uint_impl!` /
  `int_impl!` are turned into `impl __uint` / `impl __int` and added to the u8 .. / i8 .. owners. Numeric types also get `Ord` /
  `PartialOrd` / `Clone` / `Hash` .. (`n.min(m)`). An impl's undetermined type argument, such as `B` in `Iterator for Map<I, F>`, is the element type.
  The type of a `thread_local!` static is `LocalKey<T>`.
- **Type argument bindings**: if the receiver is a type argument `T`, the trait methods from `impl<T: Clone>` / `where T: Show`.
- **Definition targets**: for a type with derive, `Point::default()` / `x.clone()` go to the derive name rather than the std trait declaration (hover shows
  the trait method signature, and references count it too). `let h: Hidden = n.into();` goes to from in Hidden's `impl From<i32> for Hidden`.
  When methods with the same owner and same name in a library exist in several files (`From` impls), the first one is used.
- **Struct shorthand** `T { x }`: definition gives both the local and the field, documentHighlight gives both, and rename uses the expanding form
  (`x: new` / `new: x`). Completion after `.` does not offer associated functions that do not take self.
- **Long signatures**: symbol details were cut at 120 characters, so the return type of functions with many parameters was lost
  (now up to 1,000 characters). Also fixed a bug where a truncated signature crashed the std index thread; if building the index for one std file
  fails, only that file is skipped.

Results: fixture definition 462 → 465/467, references 606 → 609/629. The match average of `python3 bench/lsp_parity.py` is
synth 99.7% / fixture 97.3% / zustc 96.3% (rust-analyzer: 99.1% / 95.6% / 95.5%). ide (navigate.rs; its text changes during the work,
so the positions differ every time) is 95–98% (rust-analyzer 95–98%). Times are unchanged (references p50 is 5.4 ms for zustc,
27.9 ms for rust-analyzer). references of std methods (`Iterator::map` and so on) count about 80% of rust-analyzer's (before: 0).

# 型推論の不足を詰める (2026-11-18)

日付: 2026-11-18

rust-analyzer の hover の型を正解にして、よく書く式 39 個 (繰り返しの鎖・Option / Result・HashMap・タプル・
ターボフィッシュ・数の型のメソッド) を比べた。前は 17 個のうち 7 個しか合っていなかった (`Option<U>` /
`Option<Iter<'_, ..>::Item>` / 型が出ない) のが、39 個全部 (クロージャの型の表示も) 同じになった。この比べ方は
`crates/analyzer/tests/lsp.rs` の `type_inference_like_rust_analyzer` (本物の std を使う) に残した。

- **繰り返しの要素の型** (`iter_item`): `Iter<'_, T>` → &T、`IterMut` → &mut T、`IntoIter` → T、HashMap の
  `Iter<'_, K, V>` → (&K, &V)、`Map<I, impl FnMut(..) -> R>` → R、`FilterMap` / `FlatMap` / `Flatten` / `Enumerate` /
  `Zip` / `Cloned` / `Copied` / `Rev` / `Skip` .. 、`Chars` / `Lines` / `Range` ..。`Self::Item` / `<A as Iterator>::Item` /
  `U::IntoIter` の射影を置き換える (`norm_proj`)。
- **メソッドの型引数をクロージャから決める**: 定義に、シグネチャの `F: FnMut(Self::Item) -> B` などから
  (引数の番号, 型引数, 戻り値の形, 引数の形) を持たせる (`fn_bounds`)。呼び出しの引数のクロージャの戻り値の型を形に
  当てはめて (`unify`: `Option<U>` と `Option<char>` → U = char)、`map` / `and_then` / `filter_map` / `fold` の結果の型を
  決める。型引数そのものの引数 (`zip(other: U)`) は引数の式の型で。ターボフィッシュ (`collect::<Vec<_>>()` /
  `sum::<u32>()` / `parse::<u8>()`) は最初の型引数に (`_` は要素の型)。
- **クロージャの引数の型**: シグネチャの `F: FnOnce(&T)` の引数の形から (`KEY.with(|m| ..)` の m は &T、`fold` の 2 つめは
  要素)。分からなければ受け手の要素の型。タプルのパターン `|(k, v)|` / `for (i, x) in` / `let (a, b) =` も。
- **式の型**: タプルの式 `(a, b)`・タプルの添字 `x.0` (の後の添字 `u.1[0]` も)・括弧の式・配列の式 `[a, b]` / `[x; n]`・
  単位構造体の値・`match` / `if` / ブロックの式 (腕・ブロックの最後の式の型)・`&x` の参照・ローカルのクロージャの呼び出し・
  寿命の名前を外す (`&'a str` → `&str`)。
- **std のマクロの中の impl**: slice の `Iter` などの `impl Iterator` は core のマクロの中にあって見えないので、繰り返しの型に
  Iterator を持たせる。数の型のメソッド (`wrapping_sub` / `checked_sub` / `count_ones` ..) は core の `uint_impl!` /
  `int_impl!` の本体のアイテムを `impl __uint` / `impl __int` にして、u8 .. / i8 .. の持ち主に足す。数の型には `Ord` /
  `PartialOrd` / `Clone` / `Hash` .. も (`n.min(m)`)。`Iterator for Map<I, F>` の `B` のような impl の決まらない型引数は要素の型。
  `thread_local!` の static の型は `LocalKey<T>`。
- **型引数の束縛**: 受け手が型引数 `T` なら、`impl<T: Clone>` / `where T: Show` の trait のメソッド。
- **定義の行き先**: derive がある型の `Point::default()` / `x.clone()` は std の trait の宣言より derive の名前に (hover は
  trait のメソッドのシグネチャ、参照も数える)。`let h: Hidden = n.into();` は Hidden の `impl From<i32> for Hidden` の from。
  ライブラリの同じ持ち主・同じ名前のメソッドがいくつかのファイルにあるとき (`From` の impl) は先のもの。
- **構造体の省略形** `T { x }`: definition はローカルとフィールドの両方、documentHighlight も両方、rename は書き足す形
  (`x: new` / `new: x`)。`.` の後の補完には self を取らない関連関数を出さない。
- **長いシグネチャ**: 記号の detail を 120 文字で切っていたので、引数の多い関数の戻り値の型が取れていなかった
  (1,000 文字まで)。切ったシグネチャで std の索引のスレッドが落ちていた不具合も直し、std のファイル 1 つで索引を作るのに
  失敗しても、そのファイルだけ飛ばすようにした。

結果: fixture の definition は 462 → 465/467、references は 606 → 609/629。`python3 bench/lsp_parity.py` の一致の平均は
synth 99.7% / fixture 97.3% / zustc 96.3% (rust-analyzer はそれぞれ 99.1% / 95.6% / 95.5%)。ide (navigate.rs。作業の間に
本文が変わるので位置は毎回違う) は 95〜98% (rust-analyzer 95〜98%)。時間は前と同じ (references の p50 は zustc で 5.4 ms、
rust-analyzer 27.9 ms)。std のメソッドの参照 (`Iterator::map` など) は rust-analyzer の 8 割ほどを数える (前は 0)。

# Closing the gap in references of std methods (2026-11-18)

Date: 2026-11-18

In the zustc workspace, compared the references of 20 commonly used std methods against rust-analyzer, one by one
(starting from calls in `navigate.rs`).

| Method | Before (zustc / rust-analyzer) | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `Option::map` | 214 / 246 | 266 / 266 |
| `Iterator::map` | 282 / 342 | 349 / 349 |
| `collect` / `push` / `filter` / `starts_with` / `clone` / `is_empty` / `len` / `as_str` / `contains` / `get` / `insert` / `trim` / `find` / `first` / `extend` | Differences of a few to a dozen or so | All the same |
| `ToString::to_string` | 0 / 607 | 605 / 613 |
| `Option::unwrap` / `<[T]>::iter` | 341 / 346, 812 / 822 | 345 / 346, 831 / 832 |

Main fixes:

- **Name resolution**
  - For a method that exists on both the receiver type and its Deref target, pick the one closer to the receiver (`String::len` and `str::len`). Before, there were 2 and no answer was given.
  - Look at the Deref target before traits with blanket impls (`as_ref` on `RefMut<Option<T>>` is Option's).
  - If both a trait method declaration and its blanket impl (`impl<T: Display> ToString for T`) are candidates, pick the declaration.
  - When a const or function with the same name also exists in another file or crate, pick the one in the same file or same crate (`const PRELUDE`, the test `fn run`).
  - Fixed enum variants of an alias from `use .. as PTy` being mistaken for a struct with the same name (`Path`).
- **Types**
  - Elements of nested adapters (`Peekable<Skip<Args>>`).
  - Receivers of type aliases (`type Cur = Option<..>`).
  - Projections such as `<str as ToOwned>::Owned`.
  - `I::Output` of `get(i)`.
  - Tuple struct fields (`self.0`).
  - Functions taking `&mut T` (`mem::take`).
  - Passing a function name: `and_then(str_lit)`.
  - `Some(e)`.
  - Closures whose body is `if` / `match`.
  - `&|t: &str| ..`.
  - Assignment after `let x;`.
  - Fixed qualified types (`&std::cell::RefCell<..>`) being mistaken for projections and discarded.
- **Patterns**
  - Bindings in a match arm that follows an arm whose body ends with `,` without braces (`"-O" => o.opt = true, s if ..`).
  - Match arms with `==` in the guard.
  - Bindings in the guard of `matches!(e, P(g) if g..)`.
- **Library index**
  - Kept the shape of tuple variant fields in the definition, so it is known even for libraries whose text was discarded (proc_macro2's `TokenTree::Literal(l)`).
  - Also kept hints for the result type of `macro_rules!` in the definition (`json!` → `json_internal!` → `Value`).

Still different:

- The type of `&*ptr`.
- The associated const `usize::BITS`.
- `e.to_string()` on a closure parameter (`io::Error` in `map_err(|e| ..)`).
- One place where rust-analyzer goes to the `to_string` on the impl side (the specialization in string.rs).

The match average of `python3 bench/lsp_parity.py` is the same as last time or higher:

| Target | zustc | rust-analyzer |
|---|---|---|
| synth | 99.7% | 99.1% |
| fixture | 97.3% | 95.6% |
| zustc | 96.3% | 95.5% |
| ide | 98.1% (+2.8 pts) | 97.9% |

references p50 is 4.2 ms for zustc and 24.1 ms for rust-analyzer. Adding the index of dependency crates raised memory to 66 MB (rust-analyzer: 2.4 GB).

|---|---|---|

| `Iterator::map` | 282 / 342 | 349 / 349 |

- `usize::BITS` の関連 const。
- クロージャの引数の `e.to_string()` (`map_err(|e| ..)` の `io::Error`)。

`python3 bench/lsp_parity.py` の一致の平均は前回と同じか上がった:

| 対象 | zustc | rust-analyzer |
|---|---|---|

| fixture | 97.3% | 95.6% |
| zustc | 96.3% | 95.5% |
| ide | 98.1% (+2.8 点) | 97.9% |

# Closing the remaining differences from rust-analyzer in TODO.md

Date: 2026-11-18

Work on the items left in TODO.md: zust-analyzer answers that differed from rust-analyzer, the fixture remainder, and
reference speed. Each item was reproduced in a small crate and compared with rust-analyzer's answer, then checked on
the fixture workspace (`bench/ide_golden_ra.py`) and on zustc's own sources (`bench/lsp_parity.py`).

## Type inference

- **Prefix operators.** `&*p` on a raw pointer `*const T` is `&T`; `*b` on `&T` / `Box<T>` is `T`. Leading `&` /
  `&mut` / `*` are applied to the type of the operand (only when no binary operator follows). Raw pointer annotations
  (`p: *const T`) are accepted. `unsafe { .. }` blocks are looked into like plain blocks.
- **Associated consts of primitive types.** `u32::MAX` was `char` and `i64::MIN` was `f32`: a lowercase qualifier was
  read as a module, which found the deprecated module constants `core::char::MAX` / `core::f32::MIN`. Primitive type
  names are now types, so `u32::MAX` is `u32` and `usize::BITS` is `u32` (definitions match rust-analyzer).
- **Aliases with the same head name.** `std::io::Result<T>` (= `Result<T, Error>`) was never expanded, because an alias
  whose right-hand side has the same name was skipped to avoid loops. It is now expanded when the number of type
  arguments differs, and method lookup expands the receiver until it matches the impl's arity. The `e` in
  `fs::write(..).map_err(|e| e.to_string())` is `io::Error`. Among several aliases of one name, the one in the same file,
  then the same crate, then the workspace is preferred.
- **Range loop variables.** `for k in 0..n` (without parentheses) gives `k` the type of `n`; `for k in 0..3` gives
  `i32` (rust-analyzer's default). `a..` is `RangeFrom<T>`.
- **Array values.** `["a", "b"].into_iter()` was `[&str; 2]::IntoIter`: the projection was cut at the space inside
  `[&str; 2]`. It is now `IntoIter<&str>`, and `find(|k| ..)` gives `k: &&str` (so `k.len()` is `str::len`, as in
  rust-analyzer).
- **Match arms with tuple patterns.** In `(TokenTree::Literal(x), TokenTree::Literal(y)) => ..`, the walk back from `x`
  went through the previous arm's body and stopped at its `==`. The arm's pattern span is now found first.
- **Iterators of dependencies.** serde_json's `Map::iter()` returns `map::Iter` (no type arguments). It was mixed up with
  `option::Iter<'a, A>` and then with `std::path::Iter`. A type with no type arguments returned by a method is now
  qualified with its module when the name is ambiguous, and associated types are looked up only in that module. The
  impl itself is generated by a macro, so the item type is now unknown rather than wrong (TODO.md).
- **`zustc/typeAt` at bindings.** The debug request now answers at a binding itself (patterns, parameters, closure
  parameters), not only at its uses.

## Definitions and references

- **`name!(..)` resolves to macros only.** `vec!` went to `pub mod vec`, `format!` to nothing (it collided with
  `fn fmt::format`). `format!` now has 3 references, like rust-analyzer.
- **str pattern iterators.** `s.split(',').next()` went to slice `Split::next`. The methods inside core's
  `generate_pattern_iterators!` are indexed as `__str_pat_iter` (like `uint_impl!`), and impls whose number of type
  arguments does not match the receiver are dropped.
- **Crate names.** The server tells zust-analyzer which file is each crate's root (workspace crates, std / core / alloc,
  and dependencies). `std` and `fixture` now go to the crate root, `std::collections` to `collections/mod.rs`, and the
  references of a workspace crate include `crate::`, `pub(crate)` and `super` that mean its root, as in
  rust-analyzer (7/7 for `fixture`). Library crates get their own crate number so that `mod x;` is resolved within the
  same crate.
- **`cfg(miri)`.** rust-analyzer's `cargo.cfgs` defaults to `["debug_assertions", "miri"]`, so `#[cfg(miri)]` items are
  active. zust-analyzer now does the same.
- **Names inside cfg predicates.** `test` in `#[cfg(test)]` was counted as a reference of the `#[test]` attribute
  macro. Names inside `#[cfg(..)]`, the predicate of `#[cfg_attr(..)]` and `cfg!(..)` no longer resolve.
- **Golden harness.** The ide golden test now registers crate roots and gives library files their crate numbers, as
  the server does. The fixture's small std gained the macros and attributes the fixture uses (`assert!`, `assert_eq!`,
  `vec!`, `format!`, `test`, `derive`, `Copy`), so `bench/ide_golden_ra.py` compares like with like.

## Speed

References scan each file independently. Slim files are reloaded first on the main thread; then the files are scanned
on up to 8 threads (when there are 8 or more files). On 4 cores the slow queries on zustc's own sources (methods with
common names) went from 110–230 ms to 55–205 ms.

## Results

`python3 bench/ide_golden_ra.py` (the fixture against rust-analyzer):

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| definition | 465/467 | 467/467 |
| references | 609/629 | 627/629 |
| hover | 615/636 | 633/636 |

The two references left are std modules, where rust-analyzer also counts paths inside std's sources.

`python3 bench/lsp_parity.py`:

| target | agreement (zust-analyzer / rust-analyzer) | references p50 / p90 |
|---|---|---|
| synth | 99.7% / 99.1% | 0.4 / 0.9 ms |
| fixture | 97.3% / 95.6% | 0.3 / 0.9 ms |
| zustc | 96.3% / 95.5% | 2.9 / 32.8 ms (was 4.2 / 65 ms; rust-analyzer 14.2 / 880 ms) |
| ide | 99.0% / 97.5% (+0.9; references 100%, +2.5) | 4.6 / 19.1 ms |

On the zustc target the remaining differences are the intended `Default::default` rename and one `Key` reference that
rust-analyzer counts in `crates/syntax/build.rs` (the build script's own `type Key = u128`). Memory is unchanged at
66 MB. What is left is in TODO.md.

# TODO.md の rust-analyzer との残りの違いを詰める

日付: 2026-11-18

TODO.md に残っていた項目 (zust-analyzer の答えが rust-analyzer と違うもの、fixture の残り、参照の速さ) に取り組んだ。
それぞれを小さなクレートで再現して rust-analyzer の答えと比べ、fixture のワークスペース (`bench/ide_golden_ra.py`) と
zustc 自身のソース (`bench/lsp_parity.py`) で確かめた。

## 型推論

- **前置の演算子。** 生ポインタ `*const T` への `&*p` は `&T`、`&T` / `Box<T>` への `*b` は `T`。前に付いた `&` / `&mut` /
  `*` を、演算子のかかる式の型に当てはめる (後ろに二項演算子があるときは除く)。生ポインタの注釈 (`p: *const T`) も
  受け付ける。`unsafe { .. }` のブロックも、普通のブロックと同じく中を見る。
- **組み込みの型の関連定数。** `u32::MAX` が `char`、`i64::MIN` が `f32` になっていた。小文字の修飾をモジュールとして
  読み、古いモジュールの定数 `core::char::MAX` / `core::f32::MIN` を拾っていた。組み込みの型の名前は型として扱うように
  したので、`u32::MAX` は `u32`、`usize::BITS` は `u32` (定義の行き先も rust-analyzer と同じ)。
- **同じ名前を頭に持つ別名。** `std::io::Result<T>` (= `Result<T, Error>`) が開かれていなかった。右辺が同じ名前の別名は、
  ループを避けるために飛ばしていたため。型引数の数が違えば開くようにし、メソッドを引くときは impl の型引数の数に合う
  まで受け手を開く。`fs::write(..).map_err(|e| e.to_string())` の `e` は `io::Error`。同じ名前の別名がいくつもあれば、
  同じファイル、同じクレート、ワークスペースの順に選ぶ。
- **範囲のループ変数。** 括弧のない `for k in 0..n` の `k` は `n` の型、`for k in 0..3` は `i32` (rust-analyzer の既定)。
  `a..` は `RangeFrom<T>`。
- **配列の値。** `["a", "b"].into_iter()` が `[&str; 2]::IntoIter` のままだった。射影の前の型を、`[&str; 2]` の中の空白で
  切っていた。今は `IntoIter<&str>` で、`find(|k| ..)` の `k` は `&&str` (なので `k.len()` は rust-analyzer と同じく
  `str::len`)。
- **タプルのパターンの match の腕。** `(TokenTree::Literal(x), TokenTree::Literal(y)) => ..` で、`x` から後ろへ戻ると前の
  腕の本体を越え、その `==` で止まっていた。先に腕のパターンの範囲を求めるようにした。
- **依存クレートの繰り返し。** serde_json の `Map::iter()` は `map::Iter` (型引数なし) を返す。これを `option::Iter<'a, A>`
  と、次に `std::path::Iter` と取り違えていた。メソッドが返す型引数のない型は、名前がほかと重なればモジュールで修飾し、
  関連型はそのモジュールの中だけで引く。impl そのものはマクロで作られているので、要素の型は間違いではなく「分からない」
  になった (TODO.md)。
- **束縛での `zustc/typeAt`。** デバッグ用の問い合わせが、使う所だけでなく束縛そのもの (パターン・引数・クロージャの引数)
  でも答える。

## 定義と参照

- **`name!(..)` はマクロだけに解決する。** `vec!` が `pub mod vec` に、`format!` がどこにも行かなかった
  (`fn fmt::format` と重なっていた)。`format!` の参照は rust-analyzer と同じ 3 件になった。
- **str のパターンの繰り返し。** `s.split(',').next()` が slice の `Split::next` に行っていた。core のマクロ
  `generate_pattern_iterators!` の中のメソッドを `__str_pat_iter` として索引し (`uint_impl!` と同じ)、受け手と型引数の数が
  合わない impl を外す。
- **クレートの名前。** サーバが、どのファイルが各クレートの根か (ワークスペースのクレート、std / core / alloc、依存
  クレート) を zust-analyzer に伝える。`std` と `fixture` はクレートの根へ、`std::collections` は `collections/mod.rs` へ
  行く。ワークスペースのクレートの参照には、rust-analyzer と同じく、その根を指す `crate::`・`pub(crate)`・`super` も
  入る (`fixture` で 7/7)。ライブラリのクレートには別々のクレート番号を付け、`mod x;` を同じクレートの中で解決する。
- **`cfg(miri)`。** rust-analyzer の `cargo.cfgs` の既定は `["debug_assertions", "miri"]` なので、`#[cfg(miri)]` のアイテムは
  有効。zust-analyzer も同じにした。
- **cfg の述語の中の名前。** `#[cfg(test)]` の `test` を、属性マクロ `#[test]` の参照に数えていた。`#[cfg(..)]`・
  `#[cfg_attr(..)]` の述語・`cfg!(..)` の中の名前は解決しない。
- **ゴールデンのテスト。** ide のゴールデンのテストも、サーバと同じくクレートの根を設定し、ライブラリのファイルに
  クレート番号を付ける。fixture の小さな std に、fixture が使うマクロと属性 (`assert!`・`assert_eq!`・`vec!`・`format!`・
  `test`・`derive`・`Copy`) を足し、`bench/ide_golden_ra.py` が同じ条件で比べられるようにした。

## 速さ

参照はファイルごとに独立に探す。slim なファイルを先にメインのスレッドで読み直し、そのあとファイルを最大 8 本の
スレッドで探す (ファイルが 8 個以上のとき)。4 コアで、zustc 自身のソースの遅い問い合わせ (よくある名前のメソッド) は
110〜230 ms から 55〜205 ms になった。

## 結果

`python3 bench/ide_golden_ra.py` (fixture を rust-analyzer と比べる):

| | 前 | 後 |
|---|---:|---:|
| definition | 465/467 | 467/467 |
| references | 609/629 | 627/629 |
| hover | 615/636 | 633/636 |

残った参照の 2 件は std のモジュールで、rust-analyzer は std のソースの中のパスも数える。

`python3 bench/lsp_parity.py`:

| 対象 | 一致 (zust-analyzer / rust-analyzer) | references の p50 / p90 |
|---|---|---|
| synth | 99.7% / 99.1% | 0.4 / 0.9 ms |
| fixture | 97.3% / 95.6% | 0.3 / 0.9 ms |
| zustc | 96.3% / 95.5% | 2.9 / 32.8 ms (前は 4.2 / 65 ms。rust-analyzer は 14.2 / 880 ms) |
| ide | 99.0% / 97.5% (+0.9。references は 100%、+2.5) | 4.6 / 19.1 ms |

zustc の対象で残った違いは、意図した `Default::default` の rename と、rust-analyzer が `crates/syntax/build.rs` (ビルド
スクリプト自身の `type Key = u128`) で数える `Key` の参照 1 件。メモリは 66 MB のまま。残りは TODO.md にある。

# rustc's own UI tests as a specification suite

Date: 2026-11-18

`tests/ui` in rust-lang/rust is the closest thing Rust has to an executable specification: each file says, in header
directives, whether it must run, must check, or must be rejected (with the expected errors marked by `//~ ERROR`).
`bench/rust_ui.py` runs zustc against it and reports pass rates.

## Fetching

A git submodule would download all of rust-lang/rust, and git cannot make a submodule sparse without manual setup.
The script instead pins a commit (tag 1.100.0, `0ef1bc386`, the same commit as the rustc used here) and does a
shallow, blob-filtered, sparse clone of only `tests/ui` into `out/rust-tests`: 6 seconds and 170 MB, 20,364 test
files.

## What counts as passing

The kind of each test comes from its directives, as in rustc's compiletest:

| kind | files | passes when |
|---|---:|---|
| run-pass | 3771 | zustc builds it, it exits 0, and stdout equals `<name>.run.stdout` if that exists |
| check-pass | 3654 | `zustc check` accepts it |
| build-pass | 572 | zustc builds it |
| compile-fail (no pass/fail directive) | 11707 | `zustc check` rejects it with an error on a line an annotation points at |

Tests that need what zustc cannot be asked for are counted as not applicable: nightly `#![feature]`, auxiliary crates
(`aux-build`, `aux-crate`), `compile-flags` / `rustc-env`, `revisions`, targets other than Linux x86-64, `ignore-test`,
and compile-fail tests without annotations. Each zustc run is limited to 2 GB of address space (`prlimit`) and a
timeout; one test had taken the whole machine's memory before the limit was added.

For compile-fail, "rejected" alone was misleading. A first version counted any rejection and gave 64%. Many of
those were rejections for unrelated reasons, such as a missing type that the test did not mean to test. Requiring an
error on an annotated line (`//~` this line, `//~^` one line up per caret, `//~|` the same line as the previous
annotation) gives 31%. Rejections elsewhere are reported separately as "wrong line".

## Results

On 4 cores with 3 workers the applicable tests take 112 seconds.

| kind | applicable | pass | fail | wrong line | crash | timeout | pass rate | not applicable |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| run-pass | 2413 | 1120 | 1287 | - | 5 | 1 | 46.42% | 1357 |
| check-pass | 1807 | 831 | 972 | - | 4 | 0 | 45.99% | 1843 |
| build-pass | 135 | 64 | 69 | - | 2 | 0 | 47.41% | 354 |
| compile-fail | 7358 | 2291 | 2613 | 2428 | 23 | 3 | 31.14% | 4438 |

Two runs on the same machine gave the same set of passing tests.

## Keeping it from regressing

`bench/rust_ui_passing.txt` lists the 4306 passing tests. CI (`rust-ui` job) fetches `tests/ui` and fails if a test
on the list no longer passes; a timeout only warns. When a change makes more tests pass, `--write-baseline` rewrites
the list. The benchmark workflow also sends the pass rates and counts to the dashboard.

## What is next

The failures are the backlog for the language: `out/rust_ui_results.txt` lists every test with its result, and
`--filter` narrows a run to one area (for example `--filter tests/ui/closures`). The 34 crashes come first, since a
compiler should not panic on any input.

# rustc 自身の UI テストを仕様のテスト集にする

日付: 2026-11-18

rust-lang/rust の `tests/ui` は、Rust にとって実行できる仕様にいちばん近いもの。各ファイルが、頭の指示で、実行できる
べきか、検査を通るべきか、拒まれるべきか (期待するエラーは `//~ ERROR` で印を付ける) を書いている。
`bench/rust_ui.py` は zustc をそれに対して走らせ、通った割合を出す。

## 取り方

git submodule にすると rust-lang/rust 全体を取ってきてしまい、submodule を部分 checkout にするには手で設定が要る。
そこでスクリプトがコミット (タグ 1.100.0、`0ef1bc386`。ここで使っている rustc と同じコミット) を固定し、`tests/ui`
だけを、浅く・blob を絞った部分 clone で `out/rust-tests` に取る。6 秒、170 MB、テストのファイルは 20,364。

## 何を通ったとするか

各テストの種類は、rustc の compiletest と同じく指示から決める:

| 種類 | ファイル | 通ったとする条件 |
|---|---:|---|
| run-pass | 3771 | zustc がビルドでき、終了コード 0 で、`<名前>.run.stdout` があればそれと同じものを出す |
| check-pass | 3654 | `zustc check` が通す |
| build-pass | 572 | zustc がビルドできる |
| compile-fail (pass / fail の指示がない) | 11707 | `zustc check` が、注釈の指す行にエラーを出して拒む |

zustc に求められないものが要るテストは「対象外」に数える: nightly の `#![feature]`、補助のクレート
(`aux-build`・`aux-crate`)、`compile-flags` / `rustc-env`、`revisions`、Linux x86-64 以外のターゲット、
`ignore-test`、注釈のない compile-fail。zustc の 1 回の実行は、アドレス空間 2 GB (`prlimit`) と時間で制限する。
制限を付ける前は、1 つのテストがマシン全体のメモリを使い切った。

compile-fail は「拒んだ」だけでは当てにならなかった。最初の版はどんな拒み方でも数えて 64% になった。その多くは、
テストが確かめたいのとは関係のない理由 (見つからない型など) で拒んでいた。注釈の行 (`//~` はその行、`//~^` は
`^` 1 つにつき 1 行上、`//~|` は前の注釈と同じ行) にエラーを出すことを条件にすると 31%。ほかの行だけで拒んだものは
「行が違う」として別に数える。

## 結果

4 コア・3 並列で、対象のテストに 112 秒かかる。

| 種類 | 対象 | 通った | 失敗 | 行が違う | クラッシュ | 時間切れ | 通った割合 | 対象外 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| run-pass | 2413 | 1120 | 1287 | - | 5 | 1 | 46.42% | 1357 |
| check-pass | 1807 | 831 | 972 | - | 4 | 0 | 45.99% | 1843 |
| build-pass | 135 | 64 | 69 | - | 2 | 0 | 47.41% | 354 |
| compile-fail | 7358 | 2291 | 2613 | 2428 | 23 | 3 | 31.14% | 4438 |

同じマシンで 2 回走らせ、通ったテストの集合は同じだった。

## 後退させないために

`bench/rust_ui_passing.txt` は通った 4306 のテストの一覧。CI (`rust-ui` のジョブ) が `tests/ui` を取ってきて、一覧の
テストが通らなくなれば失敗する (時間切れは警告だけ)。変更で通るテストが増えたら、`--write-baseline` で一覧を
書き直す。ベンチマークのワークフローも、通った割合と数をダッシュボードに送る。

## 次にやること

失敗したものが言語の残りの仕事の一覧になる: `out/rust_ui_results.txt` にすべてのテストの結果があり、`--filter` で
1 つの分野に絞って走らせられる (例: `--filter tests/ui/closures`)。コンパイラはどんな入力でも panic するべきでは
ないので、34 件のクラッシュから先に直す。
